sectionsContent.title: Vector Addition

concept.summary: To add vectors, break each one into an x-part and a y-part, add the x-parts together and the y-parts together, then rebuild one resultant from those two totals. When the vectors already point along the axes, the components are given to you and the Pythagorean theorem finishes the job.
keyIdeas: A resultant is not finished until it has a magnitude and a direction.
The calculator's inverse tangent only returns angles between −90° and 90°. Use your sketch to decide which quadrant the resultant is really in.

items: A vector has a magnitude and a direction, and vectors are drawn tip-to-tail (S2.1).
SOH CAH TOA, with the calculator in degree mode.

sectionsContent.directions: Work every problem in your Hayden-McNeil notebook. Start each one with a tip-to-tail sketch. +x is east and +y is north. Some directions are given on the 0–360° scale, measured counterclockwise from east (east is 0°, north is 90°, west is 180°, south is 270°). Others are compass directions, like 35° north of east or 20° west of south. Convert every compass direction to the 0–360° scale before you find components. Give every resultant as a magnitude with units and an angle on the 0–360° scale, rounded to the nearest degree.

questions.prompt: Seaspray, the Autobot hovercraft, heads straight east across a river at 6.0 m/s, while the current pushes him south at 2.5 m/s. He forgot to steer against it. Find Seaspray's resultant velocity: magnitude and direction.
questions.solution:
Components: vx = +6.0 m/s, vy = −2.5 m/s.
v = √(6.0² + 2.5²) = √(36 + 6.25) = √42.25 = 6.5 m/s.
Reference angle = inverse tan of (2.5 / 6.0) = 22.6° south of east.
Quadrant IV, so θ = 360° − 22.6° = 337.4°, rounded to 337°.

steps.note: that points north of east; the current pushes south

questions.prompt: Starscream crash-landed in a ditch and is too proud to ask for help. Optimus Prime pulls him north with a force of 840 N while Bumblebee pulls west with 350 N. Find the resultant force on Starscream: magnitude and direction.
questions.solution:
Components: Fx = −350 N, Fy = +840 N.
F = √(350² + 840²) = √(122 500 + 705 600) = √828 100 = 910 N.
Reference angle = inverse tan of (840 / 350) = 67.4° north of west.
Quadrant II, so θ = 180° − 67.4° = 112.6°, rounded to 113°.

steps.note: reference angle, measured up from west
that is measured from west, not from east

questions.prompt: Jetfire fires his main thruster, giving an acceleration of 4.5 m/s² toward the south, while a damaged side thruster adds 2.0 m/s² toward the west. Ratchet told him to get that fixed. Find Jetfire's resultant acceleration: magnitude and direction.
questions.solution:
Components: ax = −2.0 m/s², ay = −4.5 m/s².
a = √(2.0² + 4.5²) = √(4.00 + 20.25) = √24.25 = 4.92 m/s², which is 4.9 m/s² to two significant figures.
Reference angle = inverse tan of (4.5 / 2.0) = 66.0° south of west.
Quadrant III, so θ = 180° + 66.0° = 246.0°, rounded to 246°.

steps.note: reference angle, measured down from west

questions.prompt: Bumblebee drives 20.0 m at 35° north of east, then swerves and drives another 9.0 m at 27° to get around a Decepticon roadblock. Find his resultant displacement: magnitude and direction.
questions.solution:
Convert to the 0–360° scale. A: 35° north of east = 0° + 35° = 35°; B: 27° is already on the 0–360° scale.
A: Ax = 20.0 cos 35° = 16.38 m, Ay = 20.0 sin 35° = 11.47 m.
B: Bx = 9.0 cos 27° = 8.02 m, By = 9.0 sin 27° = 4.09 m.
Rx = 24.40 m, Ry = 15.56 m.
R = √(24.40² + 15.56²) = 28.94 m, which is 29 m to two significant figures.
θ = inverse tan of (15.56 / 24.40) = 32.5°, rounded to 33°. Quadrant I, no adjustment.
questions.finalAnswer: 29 m at 33° (R = 28.94 m, θ = 32.5° before rounding)

row: B: 27° is already on the 0–360° scale

steps.note: adding magnitudes only works for vectors pointing the same way

questions.prompt: Wheeljack walks 45 m at 30° west of north, then 30 m at 20° south of west, looking for the bolt that fell off his latest invention. Find his resultant displacement: magnitude and direction.
questions.solution:
Convert to the 0–360° scale. A: 30° west of north = 90° + 30° = 120°; B: 20° south of west = 180° + 20° = 200°.
A: Ax = 45 cos 120° = −22.50 m, Ay = 45 sin 120° = 38.97 m.
B: Bx = 30 cos 200° = −28.19 m, By = 30 sin 200° = −10.26 m.
Rx = −50.69 m, Ry = 28.71 m.
R = √(50.69² + 28.71²) = 58.26 m, which is 58 m.
Reference angle = inverse tan of (28.71 / 50.69) = 29.5°.
Rx negative, Ry positive: quadrant II, so θ = 180° − 29.5° = 150.5°, rounded to 150°.
questions.finalAnswer: 58 m at 150° (R = 58.26 m, θ = 150.5° before rounding)

steps.note: 30° is measured from north, not from east
the calculator's answer; R_{x} < 0 puts it in quadrant II

questions.prompt: Jazz drives 65 m at 60° south of east, then 40 m at 35°, chasing Frenzy through a parking garage. Find his resultant displacement: magnitude and direction.
questions.solution:
Convert to the 0–360° scale. A: 60° south of east = 360° − 60° = 300°; B: 35° is already on the 0–360° scale.
A: Ax = 65 cos 300° = 32.50 m, Ay = 65 sin 300° = −56.29 m.
B: Bx = 40 cos 35° = 32.77 m, By = 40 sin 35° = 22.94 m.
Rx = 65.27 m, Ry = −33.35 m.
R = √(65.27² + 33.35²) = 73.29 m, which is 73 m.
Reference angle = inverse tan of (33.35 / 65.27) = 27.1°.
Rx positive, Ry negative: quadrant IV, so θ = 360° − 27.1° = 332.9°, rounded to 333°.
questions.finalAnswer: 73 m at 333° (R = 73.29 m, θ = 332.9° before rounding)

row: B: 35° is already on the 0–360° scale

questions.prompt: Optimus Prime sends Jetfire on a scouting run: 2.5 km at 60°, then 4.0 km at 30° north of west, then 1.5 km at 20° west of south. Ratchet needs to know where to send the repair crew. Find Jetfire's resultant displacement: magnitude and direction.
questions.solution:
Convert to the 0–360° scale. A: 60° is already on the 0–360° scale; B: 30° north of west = 180° − 30° = 150°; C: 20° west of south = 270° − 20° = 250°.
A: Ax = 2.5 cos 60° = 1.250 km, Ay = 2.5 sin 60° = 2.165 km.
B: Bx = 4.0 cos 150° = −3.464 km, By = 4.0 sin 150° = 2.000 km.
C: Cx = 1.5 cos 250° = −0.513 km, Cy = 1.5 sin 250° = −1.410 km.
Rx = −2.727 km, Ry = 2.756 km.
R = √(2.727² + 2.756²) = 3.877 km, which is 3.9 km.
Reference angle = inverse tan of (2.756 / 2.727) = 45.3°.
Quadrant II, so θ = 180° − 45.3° = 134.7°, rounded to 135°.
questions.finalAnswer: 3.9 km at 135° (R = 3.877 km, θ = 134.7° before rounding)

row: A: 60° is already on the 0–360° scale

steps.note: west of south turns from south toward west, so subtract from 270°

questions.prompt: Bumblebee, Ironhide, and Jazz each hook a cable to the same Energon cube and pull. Bumblebee pulls with 150 N at 20°, Ironhide with 210 N at 45° north of west, and Jazz, who would rather be dancing, with 180 N at 15° west of south.
parts: Find the resultant force on the Energon cube: magnitude and direction.
Megatron grabs a fourth cable and pulls so that all four forces add to zero, holding the cube in place. Give his force: magnitude and direction.
questions.solution:
Convert to the 0–360° scale. B: 20° is already on the 0–360° scale; I: 45° north of west = 180° − 45° = 135°; J: 15° west of south = 270° − 15° = 255°.
B: Bx = 150 cos 20° = 140.95 N, By = 150 sin 20° = 51.30 N.
I: Ix = 210 cos 135° = −148.49 N, Iy = 210 sin 135° = 148.49 N.
J: Jx = 180 cos 255° = −46.59 N, Jy = 180 sin 255° = −173.87 N.
Rx = −54.13 N, Ry = 25.93 N.
(a) R = √(54.13² + 25.93²) = 60.01 N, which is 60.0 N. Reference angle = inverse tan of (25.93 / 54.13) = 25.6°. Quadrant II, so θ = 180° − 25.6° = 154.4°, rounded to 154°.
(b) Megatron supplies the opposite of the resultant: same magnitude, direction turned 180°. 60.0 N at 154.4° + 180° = 334.4°, rounded to 334°. Components +54.13 N, −25.93 N.

row: B: 20° is already on the 0–360° scale

steps.note: a minus sign on the angle does not reverse the vector

equations.note: components of vector A at its angle
equations.plain: Ax = A cos(angle)     Ay = A sin(angle)
Rx = Ax + Bx + Cx     Ry = Ay + By + Cy

equations.note: reference angle, then fix the quadrant from your sketch
